stem: In a circle of radius ${=r1}$ cm, an arc of measure ${=m}^\circ$ has length ${=a1}\pi$ cm. Find the length of the arc of the same measure ${=m}^\circ$ in a circle of radius ${=r2}$ cm. Give the answer in terms of $\pi$.
solution: Both arcs have the same measure, so each is the fraction $\frac{{=m}}{360}$ of its own circle.
Circumference of the second circle $=2\pi\times {=r2} = {=2*r2}\pi$ cm.
Check: arcs of equal measure have lengths in the ratio of the radii: ${=a1}\pi : {=a2}\pi = {=r1} : {=r2}$.
notes: No book question supplied; parent_question_id empty. Compares equal-measure arcs in different circles. All a1, a2 are whole numbers.
